observations.text: Rowan has been postponing email replies and avoiding conversations about the return date.
Rowan reported several weeks of low mood and reduced interest in usual activities.
Rowan's worry increases about returning to work after a recent leave, prompting care.
Rowan reported fragmented sleep, waking in the night and checking the time repeatedly.
Rowan described delaying a reply to a work message because they feared being asked for a firm return date.
Rowan arrived late after parking difficulty and left early for a previously arranged ride.
Patient said the morning got away from them and confirmed intent to attend the next visit.
Patient reported a poor night of sleep before the missed appointment.
Rowan is trying to rebuild a routine at home, and both partners described difficulty with how support was offered.
The session focused on patterns of support at home and a recent morning interaction.
Couple worked on communication practice around an anxious exchange about return-to-work progress and partner reminders.
Rowan said a weekend walk with Casey helped the evening feel less dominated by worry.
Rowan described leaving work messages unopened and identified looking at one message as a lower step.
Rowan described mood as somewhat less heavy on days with a planned activity but remained concerned about work communication.
Rowan denied a new medication-related concern requiring urgent intervention.
Rowan reported continuing sleep interruption and daytime tiredness.
Rowan continues to imagine being asked questions they cannot answer; worry was evident when discussing employment.
Rowan missed an appointment the prior week; the session addressed working through the delayed reply.
Rowan completed several small activities, including opening a work message and taking two short walks, but has not yet replied to the message.
Sleep remains interrupted.
The coping skills group on January 15 was cancelled by the clinic because of staff illness.
Thinking about work continued to make Rowan want to put things off.
Ongoing avoidance of work communication.
Casey reported Rowan had been getting out for short walks and seemed more willing to discuss the coming week.
Rowan has attempted small activities and communication practice but has not yet established a reliable routine.
Casey described mornings as still difficult and Rowan becoming quiet when work comes up.
Some improvement in depressive symptoms, per clinician review.
Rowan described sleep as inconsistent.
Inconsistent sleep.
Rowan became visibly tense when discussion turned to returning to the workplace and said the discussion felt difficult to manage.
Patient identified anxiety about reconnecting with work.
Rowan became anxious during group and needed an individual visit for grounding and coping review.
Persistent avoidance and disrupted sleep continue to interfere with resuming a usual work routine.
Group addressed recognizing the sequence of triggering situation, anxious prediction, physical activation, and avoidance.
Patient requested additional help and was given access to the individual clinician.
Rowan denied current suicidal thoughts and no acute safety concern was identified.
Patient drafted a message about a gradual return to work but did not send it; checking the draft repeatedly delayed the task.
No urgent safety concern was reported.
Patient reported one night of improved sleep followed by a night of prolonged wakefulness.
Rowan described concern that seeing outstanding work items would become overwhelming.
The team reviewed helping Rowan break a difficult task into a manageable first step, and avoidance will be addressed in scheduled therapy.
Rowan asked for help understanding whom to contact about a gradual return to work schedule.
Rowan described ongoing anxiety and worry about overwhelm at work and used a grounding exercise in session.
Patient continued to postpone choosing a time for the conversation with the supervisor.
No current suicidal ideation was reported.
Sleep remained uneven, with difficulty settling on nights when work-related thoughts became repetitive.
Repetitive nighttime planning affected Rowan's settling for sleep.
Patient cancelled the January 28 individual appointment due to a personal scheduling conflict.
Rowan reported opening the work calendar but delaying a follow-up conversation.
Rowan remained anxious about the work conversation but could explain the intended first step.
Anxiety remained noticeable when anticipating contact with work.
Persistent avoidance with delayed follow-up; becomes anxious when tasks expand beyond a narrowly defined action.
Rowan reports persistent difficulty sustaining usual activities and meaningful functional impact around returning to work.
Mood felt less persistently low than earlier in the month.
Session addressed communication patterns between Rowan and partner Casey around reminders and withdrawal from work-related tasks.
Patient denied current suicidal thoughts; no new acute safety issue emerged.
Sleep disruption remains an intermittent barrier to a steadier daytime routine.
